library(symcompR)

This vignette covers `sympy.categories`: objects, morphisms, their
composition, diagrams, categories, and the drawing of commutative diagrams.

## Objects and morphisms


```{r}
Ao <- Object("A"); Bo <- Object("B"); Co <- Object("C")
f <- NamedMorphism(Ao, Bo, "f"); g <- NamedMorphism(Bo, Co, "g")
g * f
morphism_domain(g * f)
codomain(g * f)
```

`IdentityMorphism()` is the identity of an object and `CompositeMorphism()`
a composition of morphisms; `components()` lists the factors and
`flatten_morphism()` replaces a composite by a single named morphism.

```{r}
Do <- Object("D"); h <- NamedMorphism(Co, Do, "h")
morphism_name(f)
IdentityMorphism(Ao)
codomain(IdentityMorphism(Ao))
cm <- CompositeMorphism(f, g)
components(cm)
flatten_morphism(h * g * f, "u")
```

## Diagrams and categories

A `Diagram` has premises (the morphisms that are given) and conclusions
(the morphisms that are claimed to exist), each with a set of properties.

```{r}
d <- Diagram(list(f, g))
premises(d)
conclusions(d)
diagram_objects(d)
hom(d, Ao, Bo)
is_subdiagram(Diagram(list(f, g, h)), d)
d2 <- Diagram(list(list(f, "unique"), list(g, "unique")),
              list(list(g * f, "unique")))
conclusions(d2)
subdiagram_from_objects(d2, FiniteSet(Ao, Bo))
K <- Category("K", FiniteSet(Ao, Bo), list(d))
K
category_objects(K)
commutative_diagrams(K)
```

## Drawing diagrams

`DiagramGrid()` places the objects of a diagram on a grid, and
`xypic_draw_diagram()` renders the diagram as Xy-pic code for LaTeX.
`XypicDiagramDrawer()` is the drawer object behind it, and
`ArrowStringDescription()` describes one arrow.

```{r}
grid <- DiagramGrid(Diagram(list(f, g)))
grid$width
grid$height
grid_get(grid, 1, 1)
cat(xypic_draw_diagram(Diagram(list(f, g))), "\n")
class(XypicDiagramDrawer())
cat(format(ArrowStringDescription("mm", "", 0, "", "", "d", "r", "_", "f")), "\n")
```
